title: Almost Bayesian: Dynamics of SGD Through Singular Learning Theory
claim: Training dynamics deviate from the standard random-walk baseline, showing anomalous diffusion: faster-than-reference early, slower late, with fitted exponent below the baseline.
layout: single line plot, solid curve vs dashed reference, annotation box at bottom-left
description: A single matplotlib line plot titled 'Average SGD displacement over normalized time'. The x-axis is normalized time from 0 to 1. The y-axis is R(t) = sqrt(MSD(t)), running from about 2 to 11. A solid blue curve, 'Average R(t)', rises steeply at first and stays above a dashed black Brownian reference curve (α = 0.5). It then flattens into a concave, saturating shape. The two curves meet at t = 1. The legend sits at top left. A small boxed annotation at bottom left reads 'Fitted displacement exponent α: 0.441'. Light grid lines run behind the curves. The eye goes first to the gap between the blue and dashed curves. The palette is minimal: blue, black and white.
caption: Mean weight displacement of a collection of fully connected neural networks trained using SGD on a randomly generated Moons dataset (Pedregosa et al., 2011), compared with expected displacement in the case of Brownian motion. It can be seen that this displays anomalous diffusion corresponding to early super-diffusion followed by late stage sub-diffusion.
abstract: The nature of the relationship between Bayesian sampling and stochastic gradient descent in neural networks has been a long-standing open question in the theory of deep learning. We shed light on this question by modeling the long runtime behaviour of SGD as diffusion on porous media. Using singular learning theory, we show that the late stage dynamics are strongly impacted by the degeneracies of the loss surface. From this we are able to show that under reasonable choices of hyperparameters for vanilla SGD, the local steady state distribution of SGD (if it exists) is effectively a tempered version of the Bayesian posterior over the weights which accounts for local accessibility constraints.
